> **Estimated Infra Cost:** ~$19,500/month  
> **Target SLA:** 99.95% · **RTO:** 15 min · **RPO:** 5 min

## 1. System Overview

The Memory Host is a **real-time voice memory card game** built with a microservices architecture. The current local deployment uses four services (PostgreSQL, REST API, Game Engine + Signaling, Next.js frontend). This document describes the production-grade **AWS architecture** designed to scale from a local prototype to **1 million users with 100K daily active users** and **10K peak concurrent sessions**.

### Core Services

| Service | Local Port | AWS Service | Purpose |
|---------|-----------|-------------|---------|
| PostgreSQL | 5432 | **Aurora PostgreSQL** | Session data, rounds, leaderboard |
| REST API | 8000 | **ECS Fargate** | CRUD for sessions, leaderboard, health |
| Game Engine | 3002 | **ECS Fargate** | Pipecat voice pipelines (STT → Game Logic → TTS) |
| Signaling Server | 3001 | **ECS Fargate** | SmallWebRTC WebSocket relay |
| Frontend | 3000 | **ECS Fargate** | Next.js SSR + BFF proxy |
| TURN Server | — | **EC2 (Coturn)** | WebRTC NAT traversal |
| Cache | — | **ElastiCache Redis** | Session cache, leaderboard cache, rate limiting |

### External Dependencies

| Service | Purpose | Scaling Notes |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **Deepgram** | STT (Nova-2) + TTS (Aura-2) | ~100K API calls/peak hour; provisioned throughput |
| **Google STUN** | WebRTC ICE candidates | Free, built into browser |

## 2. Traffic Profile & Scaling Assumptions

### User Distribution

| Metric | Value | Calculation |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| Total registered users | **1,000,000** | Target |
| Daily Active Users (DAU) | **100,000** | 10% of total |
| Peak concurrent users | **10,000** | 10% of DAU (during peak hour) |
| Average session duration | **3–5 minutes** | Game play + WebRTC connection |
| Daily game rounds | **500,000** | ~5 rounds per active user |
| Peak requests/second (API) | **~2,000 RPS** | Game state polling (2s intervals) |
| Peak WebRTC streams | **10,000** | 1:1 bot-client per session |

### Bandwidth Estimates

| Traffic Type | Per Session | Peak Bandwidth |
|-------------|-------------|----------------|
| WebRTC audio (Opus) | ~40 Kbps uplink | ~400 Mbps peak (10K sessions) |
| API calls (JSON) | ~2 KB per poll | ~32 Mbps peak (2K RPS) |
| TTS audio (downlink) | ~64 Kbps per bot | ~640 Mbps peak |
| **Total peak** | | **~1 Gbps outbound** |

### Growth Assumptions

- Month-over-month growth: **15%** for first 6 months
- User acquisition cost amortized over 12 months
- Peak hours: **7–10 PM local time** (gaming prime time)
- Geographic distribution: 60% US/EU, 40% rest of world

## 4. Layer 1: User & Edge

### Route 53 — DNS & Routing

- **Records:**
  - `app.thememoryhost.com` — CloudFront distribution
  - `api.thememoryhost.com` — ALB (internal)
  - `signaling.thememoryhost.com` — NLB (WebSocket)
- **Routing Policy:** Latency-based routing
- **Health Checks:** Every 30s against ALB and CloudFront origins
- **Failover:** Active-passive with secondary region (eu-central-1)
- **TTL:** 60 seconds for rapid failover

### CloudFront — Content Delivery Network

- **Origins:**
  1. ALB → Next.js frontend (dynamic content)
  2. S3 bucket → static assets (images, fonts, favicons)
- **Behaviors:**
  - `/api/*` → ALB origin (no caching, all methods)
  - `/game/*` → ALB origin (no caching)
  - `/leaderboard` → ALB origin (TTL: 10s cache)
  - `/static/*` → S3 origin (TTL: 1 year, immutable)
  - `Default (*)` → ALB origin (TTL: 0, dynamic SSR)
- **SSL:** Custom SSL certificate (AWS Certificate Manager)
- **Minimum Protocol:** TLS 1.2
- **Price Class:** Use Only North America and Europe (Price Class 100) — cost optimization
- **WAF Integration:** Web ACL attached to CloudFront distribution

### WAF — Web Application Firewall

- **Rate-based rules:**
  - 2,000 requests per 5 minutes per IP (general API)
  - 100 requests per 5 minutes per IP (session creation endpoint)
- **Managed rule groups:**
  - AWS Managed Core Rule Set (SQL injection, XSS, etc.)
  - AWS Managed Anonymous IP List (block known bad actors)
  - AWS Managed IP Reputation List
- **Custom rules:**
  - Block non-browser User-Agents on `/game/` and `/leaderboard`
  - Allow only OPTIONS, GET, POST, PUT, DELETE methods
  - Geographic restriction: block high-risk regions (optional)

### DDoS Protection — AWS Shield

- **Standard:** Free, always-on protection (L3/L4)
- **Advanced:** Recommended for production ($3,000/month) — includes:
  - Enhanced DDoS visibility via CloudWatch
  - DDoS Cost Protection (credit for scaling costs during attacks)
  - 24/7 access to DDoS Response Team (DRT)

## 5. Layer 2: Application Layer (ECS Fargate)

### VPC Architecture

| Component | Configuration |
|-----------|---------------|
| VPC CIDR | `10.0.0.0/16` |
| Availability Zones | 3 (`eu-west-1a`, `eu-west-1b`, `eu-west-1c`) |
| Public Subnets | `/24` each (for ALB/NLB, NAT Gateways) |
| Private Subnets | `/20` each (for ECS tasks, RDS, Redis) |
| NAT Gateways | 1 per AZ (3 total) |
| VPC Endpoints | S3 Gateway Endpoint, ECR API/ECR DKR Interface Endpoints |

### ECS Cluster Configuration

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Launch Type | **FARGATE** |
| Platform Version | **1.4.0** (Linux) |
| CPU Architecture | **ARM64** (Graviton) — 20% cost savings vs x86 |
| Container Runtime | Docker (via ECR) |
| Task Networking | **awsvpc** (each task gets its own ENI) |
| Service Discovery | AWS Cloud Map (for signaling → game engine) |

### Service Definitions

#### Service 1: Next.js Frontend

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Tasks (desired) | **12** |
| Min / Max | 6 / 24 |
| CPU | 2 vCPU (ARM64) |
| Memory | 4 GB |
| Container Port | 3000 |
| Target Group | ALB → `/*` |
| Health Check | `/api/health` (every 30s) |
| Auto Scaling | CPU > 70% + Memory > 80% |
| Scaling Cooldown | 120s scale-out, 300s scale-in |

#### Service 2: REST API

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Tasks (desired) | **8** |
| Min / Max | 4 / 16 |
| CPU | 2 vCPU (ARM64) |
| Memory | 4 GB |
| Container Port | 8000 |
| Target Group | ALB → `/api/*` |
| Health Check | `/api/health` (every 15s) |
| Auto Scaling | CPU > 60%, Request count per target > 200 |
| DB Connection Pool | 20 connections per task (160 total writer) + read replicas |

#### Service 3: Signaling Server

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Tasks (desired) | **6** |
| Min / Max | 4 / 12 |
| CPU | 1 vCPU (ARM64) |
| Memory | 2 GB |
| Container Port | 3001 (WebSocket) |
| Target Group | NLB → `:3001` (TCP, stickiness enabled) |
| Health Check | TCP health check (every 10s) |
| Stickiness | Source IP (required for WebSocket rooms) |
| Connections per task | ~1,700 WebSocket connections |

**Connection Math:**
- 10K peak concurrent sessions
- Each signaling server task handles ~1,700 WebSocket connections
- 6 tasks × 1,700 = 10,200 capacity (with headroom)
- Each connection is lightweight — ~50 KB RAM overhead

#### Service 4: Game Engine (Pipecat Bots)

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Tasks (desired) | Variable (1 bot pipeline ≈ 1 session) |
| Min / Max | 100 / 300 |
| CPU | 4 vCPU (ARM64) |
| Memory | 8 GB |
| Container Port | 3002 (internal HTTP) |
| Target Group | Internal (Cloud Map) — not exposed to LB |
| Health Check | `/health` (every 5s — critical for bot lifecycle) |
| Auto Scaling | By SQS queue depth (incoming session requests) |

**Bot Pipeline Math:**
- Each game engine task runs **1 Pipecat bot pipeline** (Python + asyncio)
- 10K peak concurrent sessions = **10,000 bot tasks**
- Since Fargate tasks each run one bot:
  - At 4 vCPU/8 GB per bot: **10,000 tasks × $0.15/hr ≈ $1,500/hr peak**
  - This is prohibitively expensive at peak
- **Optimization:** Run **multiple bots per task** (20 bots per task):
  - 500 tasks × 20 bots = 10,000 bots
  - Each task: 4 vCPU / 8 GB (20× ~0.2 vCPU per bot)
  - Peak cost: 500 × $0.10/hr = **$50/hr**

> **Important:** Pipecat bots are asyncio-based Python processes. Each bot consumes ~200-350 MB RAM and ~0.15-0.3 vCPU when idle/active. Running 20 bots per Fargate task (4 vCPU / 8 GB) is the recommended density: 20 × 350 MB = 7 GB (leaving ~1 GB headroom for OS + supervisor process). Bots spend most time waiting on I/O (STT WebSocket, TTS HTTP, network), making multi-bot multiplexing viable.

### Auto Scaling Strategy

```
                   ┌─────────────────────┐
                   │   CloudWatch Alarm   │
                   │  (CPU > 70% for 3m)  │
                   └──────────┬──────────┘
                              │
                    ┌─────────▼─────────┐
                    │  Application Auto  │
                    │  Scaling (Target   │
                    │  Tracking)          │
                    └─────────┬─────────┘
                              │
                    ┌─────────▼─────────┐
                    │  ECS Service      │
                    │  (Adjust desired  │
                    │   count)           │
                    └───────────────────┘
```

**Cooldown Policy:**
- Scale-out: **120 seconds** between adjustments
- Scale-in: **300 seconds** between adjustments
- Use **step scaling** for rapid scale-out (+2, +4, +8 increments)

### Load Balancer Configuration

#### ALB (Application Load Balancer) — for HTTP services

| Listener | Rule | Target Group | Stickiness |
|----------|------|-------------|------------|
| `HTTPS:443` | Default (`/*`) | Next.js (`:3000`) | Disabled |
| `HTTPS:443` | Path `/api/*` | REST API (`:8000`) | Disabled |
| `HTTPS:443` | Path `/leaderboard` | REST API (`:8000`) | Disabled |
| `HTTPS:443` | Path `/health` | REST API (`:8000`) | Disabled |

#### NLB (Network Load Balancer) — for WebSocket Signaling

| Listener | Target Group | Protocol | Stickiness |
|----------|-------------|----------|------------|
| `TCP:3001` | Signaling (`:3001`) | TCP | Source IP (enabled) |
| `TCP:443` | Signaling (`:3001`) | TCP | Source IP (enabled) |

## 6. Layer 3: Data & Persistence

### Aurora PostgreSQL — Primary Database

#### Cluster Configuration

| Parameter | Writer | Reader |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| Instance class | `db.r7g.large` (2 vCPU / 16 GB) | `db.r7g.large` × 5 |
| Storage | gp3, 500 GB, 3000 IOPS | Same |
| Multi-AZ | Yes (1 standby) | Yes (spread across AZs) |
| Auto-scaling | Storage auto-grow (up to 64 TB) | Reader auto-scale |
| Backup | 35-day retention, automated | — |
| Encryption | AWS KMS (AES-256) | Same |

#### Connection Pooling — RDS Proxy

- **RDS Proxy:** Enabled for both writer and reader endpoints
- **Max connections:** 1000 (proxy) → 200 (database)
- **Idle timeout:** 10 minutes
- **Benefits:**
  - Connection multiplexing (1000s of Fargate connections → 200 DB connections)
  - Automatic failover handling
  - IAM authentication support

#### Read/Write Split

```
┌─────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐
│  Next.js │────▶│  REST API   │────▶│ Aurora Writer    │
│  Frontend│     │  (BFF)      │     │ (session create, │
│          │     │              │     │  score write)     │
└─────────┘     └──────────────┘     └──────────────────┘
                      │
                      │ reads (leaderboard, polls)
                      ▼
               ┌──────────────┐
               │ Aurora Reader│ × 5
               │ (read-only)  │
               └──────────────┘
```

**Write Operations (→ Writer):**
- Session creation
- Score updates (end of each round)
- Game end state

**Read Operations (→ Reader):**
- Leaderboard queries (polled every 10s by frontend)
- Session state polling (every 2s during game)
- Historical game data

#### Read Replica Scaling

| Metric | Threshold | Action |
|--------|-----------|--------|
| Reader CPU > 70% | 3 minutes | Add 1 reader (max 8) |
| Reader connections > 100 | 3 minutes | Add 1 reader |
| Replica lag > 1s | Immediate | Alert + route reads to writer temporarily |

### ElastiCache Redis — Caching Layer

#### Cluster Configuration

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Node type | `cache.r7g.large` (2 vCPU / 13 GB) |
| Shards | **3** (data partitioned) |
| Replicas per shard | 1 |
| Total memory | ~39 GB (3 × 13 GB) |
| Eviction policy | `allkeys-lru` (except leaderboard keys) |

#### Cache Use Cases

| Cache Key Pattern | TTL | Purpose |
|------------------|-----|---------|
| `session:{id}` | 5 minutes | Session state (faster than polling DB) |
| `leaderboard:top` | 10 seconds | Leaderboard cache |
| `leaderboard:player:{name}` | 30 seconds | Player rank |
| `rate:ip:{addr}` | 1 minute | Rate limiting counter |
| `turn:server:available` | 5 seconds | TURN server pool |
| `deepgram:token:{id}` | 50 minutes | Cached Deepgram API tokens |

#### Data Flow: Write-Through Cache

```
Write Request → REST API → Write to Aurora → Write to Redis
                ↓
Read Request  → REST API → Read from Redis (cache hit) → Return
                              ↓ (cache miss)
                          Read from Aurora → Write to Redis → Return
```

### Amazon S3 — Object Storage

| Bucket Name | Purpose | Lifecycle Policy |
|-------------|---------|-----------------|
| `memory-host-assets` | Static assets (images, fonts, sounds) | None (retain) |
| `memory-host-logs` | Application + access logs | Transition to Glacier after 90 days |
| `memory-host-builds` | CI/CD build artifacts | Delete after 7 days |
| `memory-host-audio` | Recorded game audio (optional) | Delete after 30 days |

### Deepgram — External STT/TTS

- **Service:** Deepgram Cloud API
- **STT Model:** Nova-2 (real-time streaming)
- **TTS Model:** Aura-2 (Pandora voice, British English)
- **Estimated API calls:** ~100K/hour at peak (10K sessions × ~10 STT chunks)
- **Optimization:** Pre-warm WebSocket connections, reuse sessions
- **Failover:** Client-side retry with exponential backoff
- **Cost:** ~$0.0041/min STT + ~$0.0006/char TTS → ~$3,200/month at peak usage

### AWS X-Ray — Distributed Tracing

- **Sampling rate:** 10% of requests (100% for errors)
- **Traced services:** Next.js → REST API → Aurora
- **Annotations:** `sessionId`, `playerName`, `roundNumber`
- **Segments:** Frontend, API, Database, Game Engine, Deepgram

| Game Engine | `RoundCompleted` | SNS + DB write |
| Game Engine | `GameOver` | SNS + DB write + leaderboard update |
| CloudWatch Alarm | `ScaleUp` | SNS (ops team) |
| EventBridge Schedule | `DailyCleanup` (2 AM) | Lambda (clean stale sessions) |
| EventBridge Schedule | `LeaderboardReset` (weekly) | Lambda (archive + reset) |

### Amazon SNS — Notifications

| `memory-host-analytics` | S3 (data lake), Kinesis Firehose |

## 8. WebRTC & Signaling Architecture

### Connection Flow

```
┌──────────┐         ┌──────────────┐        ┌──────────────┐
│  User    │         │  Signaling   │        │  Game Engine │
│  Browser │         │  Server      │        │  (Bot)       │
│          │         │  (NLB:3001)  │        │              │
└────┬─────┘         └──────┬───────┘        └──────┬────────┘
     │                      │                       │
     │  1. Join Room        │                       │
     │ ────────────────────►│                       │
     │                      │  2. Bot Already       │
     │                      │     Connected         │
     │                      │──────────────────────►│
     │                      │                       │
     │  3. Create Offer     │                       │
     │ ◄────────────────────│                       │
     │                      │                       │
     │  4. SDP Offer        │                       │
     │ ────────────────────►│──────────────────────►│
     │                      │                       │
     │  5. SDP Answer       │                       │
     │ ◄────────────────────│◄──────────────────────│
     │                      │                       │
     │  6. ICE Candidates   │                       │
     │ ◄══════════════════════════════════════════► │
     │         (Direct via STUN/TURN)               │
     │                      │                       │
     │  7. ═══ WebRTC Audio ═══► (Opus, SRTP)      │
     │                      │                       │
     │  8. ◀═══ TTS Audio ════════════════          │
     │                      │                       │
```

### Signaling Server Scaling

**Challenge:** WebSocket connections are stateful (room affinity). Each user must connect to the same signaling server instance for the duration of their session.

**Solution:** NLB with source IP stickiness + consistent hashing.

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| NLB Stickiness | Source IP, duration: 1 hour |
| Max connections per task | 1,700 |
| Total tasks | 6 (scale to 12 at peak) |
| Connection memory overhead | ~50 KB per connection |
| Total RAM needed | 6 × 1700 × 50 KB ≈ 510 MB (well within 2 GB) |

### TURN Server Architecture

**Why TURN?** ~15% of users will be behind symmetric NATs that STUN cannot traverse. TURN relays media through a server.

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Software | **Coturn** (open-source TURN/STUN server) |
| Instance type | `c6i.large` (2 vCPU / 4 GB) |
| Instances | 4 (Auto Scaling Group, min: 2, max: 8) |
| Port range | 49152–65535 (16,384 ports per instance) |
| Bandwidth per instance | ~250 Mbps |
| Allocation | Static pool via Route 53 DNS (weighted) |

> **Port Allocation:** Coturn runs single-threaded per relay port range. Each instance must be configured with a **unique, non-overlapping port range** (e.g., Instance 1: 49152-53247, Instance 2: 53248-57343, etc.). Use EC2 user-data scripts with instance-specific config files to assign disjoint ranges at boot. Without this, multiple instances on the same port range will cause relay conflicts and connection failures.

**Bandwidth Math:**
- 15% of 10K sessions use TURN = 1,500 relayed sessions
- Each relayed session = ~100 Kbps (bidirectional audio)
- Total TURN bandwidth: 1,500 × 100 Kbps = **150 Mbps**
- 4 instances × 250 Mbps = 1 Gbps capacity (6.6× headroom)

### WebRTC Data Channels

In addition to audio, use DataChannels for:

| Channel Label | Purpose | Reliability |
|--------------|---------|-------------|
| `game-events` | Round start, word sequence | Reliable (ordered) |
| `user-actions` | Push-to-talk start/stop | Reliable (ordered) |
| `transcript` | STT interim results (optional UX) | Unreliable |
| `latency-ping` | Round-trip time measurement | Unreliable |

## 10. Scaling Strategy

### Vertical Scaling (First)

- **Aurora:** `db.r7g.large` → `db.r7g.xlarge` (if CPU consistently > 60%)
- **Redis:** `cache.r7g.large` → `cache.r7g.xlarge` (if memory > 70%)
- **TURN:** `c6i.large` → `c6i.xlarge` (if bandwidth > 150 Mbps per instance)

### Horizontal Scaling (Primary)

#### Application Auto Scaling

| Service | Metric | Scale-Out | Scale-In |
|---------|--------|-----------|----------|
| Frontend | CPU > 70% | +2 tasks (every 2 min) | -1 task (every 5 min) |
| REST API | CPU > 60% | +2 tasks (every 2 min) | -1 task (every 5 min) |
| Signaling | Connection count > 80% | +1 task (every 2 min) | -1 task (every 10 min) |
| Game Engine | SQS Queue depth > 100 | +10 tasks (every 1 min) | -5 tasks (every 5 min) |

#### Database Scaling

- **Aurora Readers:** Auto-scale with `TargetTrackingScaling` (CPU > 70%)
  - Min: 1 reader, Max: 8 readers
  - Scale-out: +1 every 3 minutes
  - Scale-in: -1 every 15 minutes
- **Redis:** Manual scale-up (cluster mode disabled initially, then cluster mode enabled)

### Predictive Scaling

- **Scheduled actions** (EventBridge → Application Auto Scaling):
  - **07:00 UTC:** Scale-up frontend → 12 tasks (morning peak)
  - **15:00 UTC:** Scale-up REST API → 8 tasks (afternoon users)
  - **19:00 UTC:** Scale-up game engine → 300 tasks (evening gaming peak)
  - **23:00 UTC:** Scale-in all services to minimum

## 12. Disaster Recovery & HA

### Availability Targets

| Component | Target | Strategy |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Entire system | **99.95%** (~4.3 hours downtime/year) | Multi-AZ + redundant services |
| Database | **99.99%** | Aurora Multi-AZ + automated backups |
| Application | **99.95%** | Fargate multi-AZ + auto-scaling |
| Signaling | **99.99%** | NLB + multi-AZ tasks |
| STT/TTS | **99.9%** | Deepgram SLA + client-side retry |

### Recovery Times

| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Action |
|----------|-----|-----|--------|
| Single AZ failure | < 1 min | 0 | Aurora failover, Fargate rebalances |
| Full region failure | 15 min | 5 min | Route 53 failover to eu-central-1 |
| Database corruption | 15 min | 5 min | Point-in-time recovery |
| Accidental deletion | 1 hour | 35 days | Restore from backup |
| Deepgram outage | 1 min | — | Client retry, circuit breaker |

### Backup Strategy

| Component | Frequency | Retention | Method |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| Aurora | Continuous | 35 days | Automated backups |
| Aurora | Daily | 1 year | Manual snapshots (prune older) |
| Redis | Daily (RDB) | 7 days | Snapshot to S3 |
| S3 | Cross-region replication | — | CRR to eu-central-1 |
| ECR Images | Per build | 90 days | Lifecycle policy |

### Multi-Region DR (Future)

- **Primary:** `eu-west-1` (Ireland)
- **Secondary:** `eu-central-1` (Frankfurt)
- **Replication:**
  - Aurora: Cross-Region Read Replica (promote on failover)
  - S3: Cross-Region Replication
  - Route 53: Active-passive failover with health checks
- **Caveat:** WebRTC/WebSocket sessions are lost on failover — users must reconnect

## 13. Security Architecture

### Network Security

| Layer | Control |
|-------|---------|
| VPC | Security groups + NACLs |
| ALB → Frontend | Security group: allow HTTPS (443) from CloudFront only |
| NLB → Signaling | Security group: allow TCP 3001 from 0.0.0.0/0 |
| ECS tasks | Security groups: allow only from ALB/NLB |
| Aurora | Security group: allow only from ECS tasks + RDS Proxy |
| Redis | Security group: allow only from ECS tasks |
| TURN server | Security group: allow UDP 49152-65535 from 0.0.0.0/0 |

### Data Encryption

| State | Encryption |
|-------|-----------|
| In-transit (user → CloudFront) | TLS 1.3 |
| In-transit (CloudFront → ALB) | TLS 1.2 (self-signed or ACM) |
| In-transit (ECS → Aurora) | TLS 1.2 |
| In-transit (ECS → Redis) | Encryption in transit (AUTH token) |
| At-rest (Aurora) | AWS KMS (AES-256) |
| At-rest (Redis) | Encryption at rest (KMS) |
| At-rest (S3) | SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS |
| Audio data (ephemeral) | Not persisted (RAM only) |

### IAM Roles & Permissions

| Role | Permissions | Used By |
|------|------------|---------|
| `ecsTaskExecutionRole` | ECR pull, CloudWatch logs | All ECS tasks |
| `ecsTaskRole-frontend` | S3 read (assets) | Next.js tasks |
| `ecsTaskRole-api` | Aurora access (via RDS Proxy IAM), Redis (via AUTH), S3 write (logs) | REST API tasks |
| `ecsTaskRole-engine` | Aurora access, Redis access, Deepgram API key (Secrets Manager) | Game Engine tasks |
| `ecsTaskRole-signaling` | CloudWatch logs only | Signaling tasks |
| `codebuild-role` | ECR push, S3 write, CloudWatch logs | CodeBuild |

### Secrets Management (AWS Secrets Manager)

| Secret | Rotation | Accessed By |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` | Manual | Game Engine |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | 90 days | RDS Proxy → Aurora |
| `REDIS_AUTH_TOKEN` | Manual | REST API + Game Engine |
| `DJANGO_SECRET_KEY` | Manual | REST API (FastAPI signing) |

### Security Best Practices

- **Principle of least privilege:** Each service gets minimal required permissions
- **AWS Config:** Enable with rules for:
  - `S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_READ_PROHIBITED`
  - `RDS_INSTANCE_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK`
  - `ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_LOGGING_ENABLED`
  - `CLOUDFRONT_DEFAULT_ROOT_OBJECT_CHECK`
- **GuardDuty:** Enabled for threat detection
- **Security Hub:** Aggregates findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Config

## 15. CI/CD Pipeline

### Pipeline Architecture

```
┌──────────┐   ┌───────────┐   ┌──────────┐   ┌──────────┐
│  GitHub   │──▶│ CodePipeline │──▶│ CodeBuild │──▶│   ECR    │
│  (main)   │   │            │   │          │   │          │
└──────────┘   └────────────┘   └──────────┘   └────┬─────┘
                                                      │
                                               ┌──────▼──────┐
                                               │  ECS Service │
                                               │  (Blue/Green)│
                                               └─────────────┘
```

### Pipeline Stages

| Stage | Duration | Actions |
|-------|----------|---------|
| **Source** | — | Fetch from GitHub (main branch) |
| **Build** | ~5 min | `npm ci`, `npm run build` (frontend), `pip install -r requirements.txt` (backend) |
| **Test** | ~3 min | Run unit tests, lint, typecheck |
| **Image Build** | ~3 min | Docker build + push to ECR |
| **Deploy (Staging)** | ~2 min | Update ECS service (staging cluster), run smoke tests |
| **Deploy (Production)** | ~2 min | Blue/Green deployment via ECS CodeDeploy |

### Deployment Strategy: Blue/Green

- **Blue:** Current production version
- **Green:** New version
- **Traffic shift:** 10% → 50% → 100% over 15 minutes
- **Rollback:** Automatic if CloudWatch alarm triggers during shift
- **Validation:** Post-deploy smoke tests run against green before full shift

### Rollback Procedure

1. **Manual rollback:** Revert the GitHub commit → pipeline triggers automatically
2. **Automatic rollback:** If error rate > 5% within 5 minutes of deploy:
   - CodeDeploy shifts traffic back to blue
   - SNS notification sent to #deployments
   - PagerDuty incident created

## 16. Performance Benchmarks

### Target Latencies

| Operation | Target | Degraded |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Page load (Next.js SSR) | < 200ms | < 500ms |
| API response (p50) | < 50ms | < 150ms |
| API response (p99) | < 200ms | < 500ms |
| Database query (simple) | < 5ms | < 20ms |
| Database query (leaderboard) | < 20ms | < 100ms |
| STT latency (end of speech → text) | < 500ms | < 1s |
| TTS latency (text → first audio) | < 300ms | < 800ms |
| End-to-end round trip (speak → hear) | < 1.2s | < 2.5s |
| Signaling handshake | < 500ms | < 2s |

### Load Testing Strategy

| Test Type | Target | Tool |
|-----------|--------|------|
| API load test | 2,000 RPS | Locust (Python) |
| WebSocket burst | 10K connections | artillery |
| WebRTC session | 100 concurrent | Custom script |
| Database stress | 500 concurrent queries | pgbench |
| Endurance | 24-hour steady load | Locust |

### Capacity Tests

**Single Fargate Task Capacity (Game Engine):**
- 20 bot pipelines per task (4 vCPU / 8 GB)
- Each bot: ~5% CPU, ~200 MB RAM (idle)
- Each bot: ~15% CPU, ~350 MB RAM (active — STT + TTS)
- Max active per task: ~12 bots simultaneously (3:1 active:idle ratio)
- Total capacity per task: 20 bots (mixed idle/active)
- Headroom: 8 GB - (20 × 350 MB) = ~1 GB for OS + supervisor

**Scaling Prediction:**
- 10K active users × 1 bot each = 10K bots
- 10K / 20 bots per task = **500 tasks**
- 500 × 4 vCPU = **2,000 vCPU peak**
- 500 × 8 GB = **4,000 GB RAM peak**

## 17. Migration Strategy

### Phase 1: Lift & Shift (Current → AWS)

**Estimated effort:** 2 weeks

| Step | Tasks |
|------|-------|
| 1.1 | Create VPC, subnets, security groups |
| 1.2 | Set up Aurora PostgreSQL (restore from dump) |
| 1.3 | Set up ElastiCache Redis |
| 1.4 | Build ECR repositories + push Docker images |
| 1.5 | Create ECS cluster + service definitions |
| 1.6 | Deploy Next.js frontend with BFF proxy |
| 1.7 | Deploy REST API |
| 1.8 | Deploy Game Engine + Signaling Server |
| 1.9 | Configure ALB + NLB + CloudFront |
| 1.10 | Set up Route 53 DNS |
| 1.11 | Validate end-to-end flow |

### Phase 2: Optimization (Weeks 3–4)

| Step | Tasks |
|------|-------|
| 2.1 | Enable Auto Scaling with CloudWatch alarms |
| 2.2 | Set up RDS Proxy for connection pooling |
| 2.3 | Implement Redis caching (session + leaderboard) |
| 2.4 | Configure WAF rules |
| 2.5 | Set up CI/CD pipeline (CodePipeline + CodeBuild) |
| 2.6 | Configure CloudWatch dashboard + alarms |
| 2.7 | Enable X-Ray tracing |
| 2.8 | Load test and tune scaling thresholds |

### Phase 3: Multi-Bot Optimization (Week 5) — CRITICAL PATH

> **⚠️ Warning:** This phase is **cost-critical**. Without multi-bot optimization, running 10K separate Fargate tasks (1 bot each) costs ~$45,000/month in compute alone. Multi-bot multiplexing (20 bots/task) reduces this to ~$9,200/month. This phase must be prioritized before any production scale-up beyond 1,000 concurrent users.

| Step | Tasks |
|------|-------|
| 3.1 | Refactor Game Engine to run multiple bots per process |
| 3.2 | Implement bot pool manager inside each Fargate task |
| 3.3 | Add graceful bot lifecycle (start/stop without affecting siblings) |
| 3.4 | Add SQS queue for session dispatch |
| 3.5 | Implement signaling service discovery (Cloud Map) |
| 3.6 | Load test with 10K+ concurrent bots |

### Phase 4: Production Readiness (Week 6)

| Step | Tasks |
|------|-------|
| 4.1 | Security audit + penetration testing |
| 4.2 | Disaster recovery drill |
| 4.3 | Implement RTO/RPO monitoring |
| 4.4 | Create runbooks for all critical alarms |
| 4.5 | Set up PagerDuty on-call rotation |
| 4.6 | Production cutover (Route 53 DNS flip) |
| 4.7 | Post-launch monitoring (72-hour watch) |

  desiredCount: 12,
  // ...
});

// Load Balancers
new ApplicationLoadBalancer(this, 'ALB', { vpc, internetFacing: true });
new NetworkLoadBalancer(this, 'NLB', { vpc, internetFacing: true });

// CloudFront
new Distribution(this, 'CloudFrontDist', {
  defaultBehavior: { origin: albOrigin },
  additionalBehaviors: { '/api/*': { ... } },
});

// WAF
new CfnWebACL(this, 'WebACL', { ... });
